subject: geography

moments.title: Paris Agreement adopted
moments.body: 12 December 2015: the Paris Agreement is adopted. Goal: hold global average temperature increase 'well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels' and pursue efforts to limit to 1.5°C. Each country submits its own Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), reviewed every five years (the 'ratchet mechanism').

quote.text: Today, we celebrate. Tomorrow, we have to act.
quote.attrib: Christiana Figueres, UNFCCC Executive Secretary, 12 December 2015

moments.takeaway: Paris replaced Kyoto's top-down binding model with bottom-up pledges. Every party signs; no party has binding emissions caps.

moments.title: Implementation and gaps
moments.body: The IPCC's 'Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C' (October 2018) showed the difference between 1.5 and 2°C was substantial. The US withdrew under Trump (November 2020) and rejoined under Biden (February 2021). The first Global Stocktake at COP28 (Dubai 2023) acknowledged that current NDCs are insufficient to meet the 1.5°C goal.
moments.takeaway: Climate Action Tracker assessment: even with all current pledges met, the world is on track for around 2.5-2.9°C warming by 2100.

now.title: The ratchet under strain
now.body: COP28 (Dubai 2023) agreed the first explicit call for 'transitioning away from fossil fuels'. COP29 (Baku 2024) struggled over climate finance. The 1.5°C goal is increasingly described by climate scientists as 'effectively unreachable' without rapid decline or large overshoot.
now.open_questions: Can the ratchet mechanism work fast enough? The five-year cycle was designed to enable strengthening; whether parties will deliver the required scale of strengthening is the central political question.

reflection: Paris was a diplomatic triumph and a substantive disappointment. The framework was strong enough to include every major emitter; the actual commitments remain insufficient. Both facts are part of the story.
